business_rules: Users must register with a username and password, and duplicate usernames are not allowed.
Access is denied when the user does not exist, the password is incorrect, or the stated role does not match the registration.
At least two user roles exist: regular user and administrator.
Catalog-management functions are restricted to the administrator role.
A movie title is treated as the unique identifier for catalog registration, and duplicate titles are not allowed.
A movie can belong to more than one category.
Movie registration must include at minimum title, rating, alternate title, release date, duration, director, screenplay, cast, categories, synopsis, and poster.
The system must prevent deletion of nonexistent movies.
Before a batch deletion, the system must inform the administrator which movies have been selected.
Before playback, the video file must be available in the application delivery area; if not, the system must attempt to obtain it from the configured local repository.
The standard playback process assumes that the physical movie file corresponds to the registered title.
The source movie filename must follow the pattern expected by the environment configuration for automatic loading to work.
Uploading the video file and registering the movie are related but independent steps.
The catalog must be displayed in pages of up to 12 movies.
The system must maintain a consistent response format for operations, indicating status, message, and returned data.
User, movie, and category information must be persistently stored.
The user's session must remain identified in the browser until the user logs out or clears local data.
The application's operating process must treat MP4 as the standard video format.
The system must support uploads of large video files, up to 2 GB per file.

issues.description: Catalog Service is overly coarse. It combines four distinct domain capabilities: movie catalog browsing (RF-08 to RF-12), movie details lookup (RF-13 to RF-16), category-based content discovery (RF-17 to RF-21), and catalog administration including movie registration, deletion, and large video file upload (RF-26 to RF-33, RNF-48). These capabilities have different actors (regular users vs. administrators), different change drivers, and different structural entrypoints in the existing codebase. Bundling them into one service creates a service that is not independently deployable or evolvable and weakens the boundary between read-oriented catalog discovery and write-oriented administration.

Structural analysis identifies separate HTTP entrypoints: MovieController, MovieUploadController, and TypeController.
RNF-46 restricts catalog-management functions to the administrator role, while browsing and discovery are available to regular users.
RNF-48 requires support for uploads of large video files up to 2 GB, which is a distinct operational concern from catalog browsing.
issues.recommendation: Split Catalog Service into at least two services: a Catalog Browsing Service responsible for movie listing, details lookup, and category-based discovery, and a Catalog Administration Service responsible for movie registration, deletion, and video file upload. Alternatively, if a single catalog service is retained, explicitly justify why the administration and browsing capabilities cannot evolve independently and document the internal module boundaries.

The declared direction is therefore unsupported and potentially inverted.
